projects.name: Cancer Casefinding Pipeline
projects.tagline: Hospital feeds in, one trusted record per cancer case out.
projects.problem: A hospital cancer registry receives pathology, admissions, clinical notes and billing from several systems, out of order and with mismatched identities. Output: one trusted record per cancer case, coded to NAACCR, exported for analytics.
projects.decision: A reportability ladder of SEER rules decides everything it can. A language model sees only the 61 reports no rule could decide. LLM bill: $0.0054.
highlights: Simulated three hospitals sending HL7 v2.5.1 ORU and ADT (A04, A08, A40), FHIR R4 bundles and billing CSV: 1,320 Synthea patients, 3,554 arrivals, 279 reportable cases, 287 look-alikes, 19 planted problem types, and an ICD-O-3 coding change on day 11.

Built the pipeline: quarantine with a reason per rejected message; parse and normalize; patient resolution on SSN, merge links and a demographic threshold measured clean across 5 to 10; reconciliation of documents into cases; a reportability ladder of SEER rules with a language model only for the 61 reports no rule could decide; record versioning with a test that the record survives the coding change; NAACCR flat and OMOP exports served from DuckDB.

Result: 279 records, 278 right, 0 missed, 0 duplicate cases, 0 contested; every one of 3,554 arrivals accounted for as accepted, duplicate, quarantined or non-reportable. Every planted problem caught. LLM bill $0.0054, prompts cached, rerun byte-identical in 109 s.

Built the public replay page and report page: the feed plays on load, tapping a record pins its card, every number is baked at deploy and recounted at load, checked at 375 px and 1200 px with zero console errors.

projects.name: Shelf-Scan Conflation Engine
projects.tagline: Noisy badge-camera reads in, one record per shelf spot out.
projects.problem: A badge camera worn by store staff reads shelf labels as they walk. Reads arrive damaged, duplicated and re-sent, and the product catalog changes under them. Output: one record per shelf spot, matched to the catalog and served against the planogram.
projects.decision: Measured before choosing: Haiku vs Sonnet on 696 spots. Both 0 wrong at "sure", Haiku 13.6x cheaper. LLM bill for the whole feed: $0.02.
highlights: Simulated the feed with real data: 3 stores, 7 aisles, 300 real products from Open Food Facts, 12 badge walks over 3 days, restocking between days, doubles in a frame, a second badge, re-sent frames, about 1 in 100 rows damaged, and a catalog change (3 renames, 2 new sizes with new barcodes, 1 discontinued, 1 new).

Built a 9-stage pipeline: ingest with quarantine and a reason for every dropped row; normalize; barcode and exact-text match; close spelling with the threshold read off a measured curve; same-spot and other-day evidence; a language model only for the 159 spots nothing else could name, accepted at "sure" only.

Golden record per shelf spot with survivorship by method rank (barcode > exact > close > same spot > other day > model), lineage across the catalog change, a test that the record survives the change, and DuckDB serving against the planogram with a compliance table per store, aisle and shelf.

Result: 5,927 lines in, 5,705 usable reads, 5,586 named right (97.9%), 3 wrong and none reached the record; 1,763 records, 0 wrong, 1 contested, 18 open; compliance 96.0% against a 96.5% truth, gap reconciled exactly.
Every stage scored before the next, byte-identical reruns, full run in 20 s with no API key. The report page counts every number from the data files at load.

projects.name: Robot Telemetry Pipeline
projects.tagline: Every robot message reaches the cloud once, in order, provably.
projects.problem: A hospital transport robot produces about 15,000 messages per trip across 13 sensor streams, and hospital WiFi drops in lifts. Every message must reach the cloud once, in order, provably.
projects.decision: Record every message to the robot's own disk before any transmission. The robot keeps its copy until the server confirms the checksum, so a damaged segment can be repaired.
highlights: Built a 7-stage pipeline: record every message to the robot's own disk before any transmission; transport; validate with the message id as primary key so duplicates are harmless; cold storage; refined table ordered by event time rather than arrival time.

Simulated 63 trips with 38 network blackouts, 11 duplicate deliveries and 2 files corrupted in transit. Result: 915,068 messages produced, 915,068 in cold storage, 915,068 in the refined table, none lost. Every message ends as accepted, duplicate or quarantined with a reason, and the counts sum to what arrived.
A prove script plants seven faults and checks each is caught; a page check confirms the write-up has no hardcoded numbers.

projects.name: X Reacts
projects.tagline: A live platform where creators react to videos on stream and viewers pay to take part. Designed and shipped alone.
projects.decision: The viewer's player holds 4.6 s behind the creator's live stream through pauses, seeks and resumes, using playback-rate correction instead of hard seeks.
highlights: React/Vite front end, Firebase back end, 19+ surfaces (onboarding, creator studio, viewer page, earnings and withdrawals, admin portal, real-time chat) and a mobile admin app.
Checkout, payment and virtual-currency flow on real transactions with automated splits and refunds, and client-side NSFW moderation on uploads.
Security hardening pass that moved trust from the client to the server, locked database rules and closed every identified vulnerability.

projects.name: Penn Station Transfer-Risk Forecasting
projects.tagline: Graduate project, UT Arlington. 142,844 multimodal records and 82,959 real-time arrivals into 299,186 scenarios; a 2-3 minute transfer buffer cuts failure risk from 75% to under 20%.
